subject: business-studies
title: Market Entry and Trade Blocs
welcome_lead: Pick the right entry mode - and know which trade bloc rules you face.
meta_desc: A-Level Global Business: market entry modes and trade blocs (EU, USMCA, ASEAN).
final_note: Entry mode trades risk for control; trade blocs lower tariffs but tie firms to rules.

concepts.def: Chandler (1962): determination of long-term goals and allocation of resources to achieve them.
Mission states current purpose; vision states future aspiration; both should anchor strategy.
1985: cost leadership, differentiation, focus; firms 'stuck in the middle' underperform.
Kim and Mauborgne (2005): create uncontested market space rather than competing in 'red oceans'; e.g. Cirque du Soleil.
Johnson, Scholes and Whittington: firms become misaligned with environment as historic success blinds management.
Corporate (which markets), business (how to compete), functional (operations) levels of strategic decision.

walkthroughs.body_html: Risk and control rise together: exporting is cheap and easily reversed; FDI is heavy commitment but full control; licensing and joint ventures sit in between.
Members of a bloc lower tariffs on each other and align rules. EU has free movement of goods, services, capital and people; USMCA replaced NAFTA in 2020; ASEAN spans 10 Southeast Asian states.
Cultural and political risk pushes firms toward joint ventures with local partners. Strong IP protection and capital make FDI attractive. Low margin commodity producers often stay with exporting.
